answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can vote on reputation or claim rewards. The ledger limits each locked token to one active identity, so creating a hundred accounts does not create a hundred votes: the attacker must acquire and immobilize a hundred times the stake, risking loss if later evidence proves fraud. A cedar orchard may supply useful agents, but each still needs its own stake; the shared thread of account names alone grants no influence.
